title: Cobolli dreams of the ATP Finals: “It’s like a Grand Slam”

 “I want to live those emotions on court”: Flavio Cobolli no longer hides his ambitions for the ATP Finals. After a season highlighted by a Roland-Garros final, the Italian knows how far he has come — and is aiming even higher.
 Italy's Flavio Cobolli looks on during his match against Canada's Felix Auger-Aliassime in their men's singles quarterfinal match on day 11 of the Roland-Garros tennis tournament on Court Philippe-Chatrier at the Roland-Garros complex in Paris, June 3, 2026. © ALAIN JOCARD / AFP Arthur Millot 24/10/2026, 09:12 3 min to read Follow us ATP 250 ATP Finals Cobolli Lyon Turin Flavio Cobolli still believes in qualifying for the ATP Finals in Turin.
 Through to the semifinals of the Lyon ATP 250 after his win over Brandon Nakashima (4-6, 6-4, 6-4), the Italian opened up about his end-of-season goal, as well as his 2026 season and his run at Roland-Garros.
 Remove ads “For me, it’s a dream. It’s like a Grand Slam”
 Speaking to the ATP, Cobolli made no secret of his desire to compete at the season-ending Masters tournament, held in Turin from November 15 to 22.
 For reference, he currently sits 5th in the ATP Race with 3,640 points, 130 points ahead of Daniil Medvedev in 6th (who will face Bublik in the Almaty semifinals). He is also 505 points behind the cut that qualifies players automatically for Turin.
 “ For me, it’s a dream, almost like a Grand Slam. I hadn’t really thought about the ATP Finals before, but today, I’m well positioned in the race and I’m one of the players who can qualify.
 There are still a few tournaments left to play, and I need to play as many matches as possible to get there. I don’t want to focus too much on qualifying, but rather remind myself how great and fun it would be to take part.
 It would be something truly special. I went to Turin every year, I had lunch with the players and took part in sponsor events. I got to feel all those emotions from the outside, but now I want to experience them on court,” he explained.
 His Roland-Garros final
 The Italian also gave a positive assessment of his season, highlighted in particular by his Roland-Garros final against Alexander Zverev. 
 “I think I can look back on my season very positively. So far, I’ve had an excellent year and I still have several goals to achieve, notably qualifying for the ATP Finals in Turin.
 My start to the season was difficult, like last year, but the period between the clay and the grass was extraordinary for me. Roland-Garros was a special moment.
 I would never have imagined reaching a Grand Slam final. Once you get to that stage, you do everything you can to try to win the title. I tried, but I was up against an extraordinary player who deserved the win more that day.
 At the time, I was happy to have lived that experience. Today, when I think back to that match, it hurts, but I know I will never forget it. I was lucky to be able to play in such a final,” he shared.
 “I’m lucky to have people like that by my side”
 Cobolli also stressed the importance of his team in his progress this season.
 “Work off the court matters. This year, I changed a lot of things with my team. I spent more time training and I also tried to have more fun on court.
 I also learned to listen better to my team’s advice, and I think it has paid off.
 I’m lucky to be surrounded by people like them. They genuinely care about me and want to be by my side.
 When I’m with them, I feel all their affection, and it helps me a lot in my game.”
 The fans and Italian tennis
 Finally, the Italian spoke about the fans’ support and the golden era Italian tennis is going through.
 “I have always felt the fans’ support. In Italy, we are living through an extraordinary period for tennis, with Jannik Sinner and many other players. We are truly lucky.
 We are also lucky to have a great stage like Turin. We are happy to play in front of our fans and our families.
 Last year, in Bologna, I felt an emotion I had never experienced before in my life. Winning the Davis Cup was something truly special.”
